cases.reason: A and B were created through the UI in separate persistent browser profiles with the same password; public keys differ and both vaults store encrypted key material without password/nsec fields.
Persistent browser restart restored A only when requested; B required the correct password, rejected the wrong one without vault mutation, and manual lock cleared the session.
The UI exported an encrypted backup and a clean context imported the same public identity; it could reopen the contact using the other person’s public npub.
The public key shown in B profile opened A’s conversation; a valid nprofile preserved its local relay hint and did not connect automatically.
Empty, truncated, name-only, nsec and self contacts were rejected in Portuguese without closing the dialog, creating the wrong contact or changing identity.
Across creation, lock, backup and contact flows, only localhost assets were requested; passwords/private keys were absent from Web Storage and no central login/recovery request was observed.
